report.verdict: Customer success work with a strong renewal result, tucked behind a job-seeking headline and an in-house title.
write_up: Customer success professional with a book of mid-market shipping software accounts and earlier support work. There’s enough here for a recruiter to reach out, but the headline leads with the search for a job rather than the work, and the Parcelwise title needs translating.

The renewal line is the model: it names the conversations and the 91% of accounts by revenue renewed in 2025. That result and the onboarding guide are already in your most recent job, ready to bring into the About.

Start with the headline and About, then put a recognizable title beside Customer Happiness Hero II. Add the kinds of tickets you handled at Parcelwise too. Together, those changes would let someone hiring for customer success see your account and support work without guessing what the title means.

cards.line: Open to work | Seeking new opportunities in Customer Success
cards.cannot_tell: The headline leads with what you need, not the work you do. Your mid-market accounts and shipping software work deserve that space.

cards.cannot_tell: Your About asks for an opportunity before it says what you did. The Parcelwise renewal line gives you a much stronger opening.
cards.example: I managed a book of 85 mid-market accounts for a shipping software company. I ran quarterly business reviews and renewal conversations, renewing 91% of accounts by revenue in 2025.

cards.cannot_tell: This title makes sense inside Parcelwise, but a stranger has to work out what the job is called elsewhere. Your account book and renewal work point to customer success.

Zendesk tells me where you worked on tickets, but not what customers needed help with. Someone searching for ticket triage or troubleshooting gets no match from this line.
cards.example: Answered support tickets in Zendesk for [who contacted you], including [types of issues] and [how you resolved them].
